content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions involving amikacin, a commonly used aminoglycoside antibiotic. 1. Amikacin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. This combination is contraindicated. 2. Amikacin and Cidofovir: Both drugs elevate the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Amikacin and Neomycin (oral): Concurrent use increases the likelihood of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Amikacin and Atracurium: Amikacin enhances the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Amikacin and Bacitracin: Co-administration raises the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Bacitracin should not be used concurrently with other nephrotoxic agents. 6. Amikacin and BCG Vaccine (live): Amikacin reduces the efficacy of the BCG vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Live bacterial vaccines should only be administered after completing antibiotic therapy. 7. Amikacin and Bumetanide: Both drugs increase each other’s toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to a heightened risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Amikacin and Cholera Vaccine: Amikacin antagonizes the effects of the cholera vaccine. Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics, as they may inactivate the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 9. Amikacin and Cisatracurium: Amikacin enhances the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Amikacin and Iodinated Contrast Media: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Amikacin and Cyclosporine: Both drugs elevate the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Amikacin and Ethacrynic Acid: Co-administration increases the risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Amikacin and Furosemide: Both drugs increase each other’s toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to a heightened risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Amikacin and Ioversol: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Amikacin and Oral Microbiota: Amikacin reduces the efficacy of oral microbiota products due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 16. Amikacin and Pancuronium: Amikacin enhances the effects of pancuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Amikacin and Quinidine: Quinidine increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Amikacin and Rocuronium: Amikacin enhances the effects of rocuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Amikacin and Succinylcholine: Amikacin enhances the effects of succinylcholine through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Amikacin and Tacrolimus: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Amikacin and Teicoplanin: Both drugs elevate the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Amikacin and Torsemide: Co-administration increases the risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Amikacin and Typhoid Vaccine (live): Amikacin reduces the efficacy of the typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Live bacterial vaccines should only be administered after completing antibiotic therapy. 24. Amikacin and Vecuronium: Amikacin enhances the effects of vecuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Amikacin and Botulinum Toxin A (e.g., AbobotulinumtoxinA, IncobotulinumtoxinA, LetibotulinumtoxinA): Aminoglycosides like amikacin may potentiate the effects of botulinum toxin, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Amikacin and Acyclovir: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 27. Amikacin and Adefovir: Both drugs elevate the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Amikacin and Amiodarone: Amiodarone increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Amikacin and Conjugated Estrogens: Amikacin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Amikacin and Capreomycin: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 31. Amikacin and Carboplatin: Both drugs elevate the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Amikacin and Cephalosporins (e.g., Cefaclor, Cefadroxil, Cefazolin, Cefdinir, Cefditoren, Cefepime, Cefixime, Cefotaxime, Cefotetan, Cefoxitin, Cefpirome, Cefpodoxime, Cefprozil, Ceftaroline, Ceftazidime, Ceftibuten, Ceftizoxime, Ceftobiprole, Ceftolozane, Ceftriaxone, Cefuroxime, Cephalexin, Cephaloridine): Cephalosporins may increase the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides like amikacin. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Amikacin and Cisplatin: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Amikacin and Clarithromycin: Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Amikacin and Colistin: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 36. Amikacin and Deferasirox: Acute renal failure has been reported with deferasirox. Co-administration with nephrotoxic drugs like amikacin may increase this risk. Monitor serum creatinine and/or creatinine clearance closely. 37. Amikacin and Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Amikacin reduces the levels or effects of these hormones by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and consider alternative or additional forms of birth control. 38. Amikacin and Digoxin: Amikacin reduces the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Amikacin and Dronedarone: Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Amikacin and Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Amikacin and Erythromycin (Base, Ethylsuccinate, Lactobionate, Stearate): Erythromycin increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Amikacin and Estradiol/Estradiol Valerate/Estrogens (Conjugated Synthetic, Estropipate, Mestranol): Amikacin reduces the levels or effects of these hormones by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Amikacin and Felodipine: Felodipine increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Amikacin and Foscarnet: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Amikacin and Fosphenytoin: Fosphenytoin reduces the levels or effects of amikacin by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Amikacin and Gentamicin: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 47. Amikacin and Ibuprofen (IV): Ibuprofen increases amikacin levels by reducing renal clearance. This interaction is more common in preterm infants. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Amikacin and Indinavir: Indinavir increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Amikacin and Ketoconazole/Levo-Ketoconazole: These agents increase the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Amikacin and Loratadine: Loratadine increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Amikacin and Magnesium Supplements: Co-administration enhances the neuromuscular blocking effects of both agents, potentially leading to respiratory complications. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Amikacin and Methoxyflurane: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Amikacin and Nefazodone: Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Amikacin and Nicardipine: Nicardipine increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely.
